lyrics:
[Intro: male group chanting alone, then drums and bass]
Hubba-loo, hubba-loo-la
Hubba-loo, hubba-loo-la
Hubba-loo, hubba-loo-la
Hubba-loo, hubba-loo-la

[Verse 1: joyful tenor, galloping beat, chant continues underneath]
I can't sit still, it's in my shoes
You're the best kind of terrible news
Lips like cider and a laugh like rain
I'm in trouble and I can't complain

[Chorus: brass section, full voice, group answering]
Oh, I'm stuck on a good thing
Glued to a real thing
Nobody come and pull me free
I'm stuck on a good thing
Tied to the best thing
That ever went and happened to me

[Verse 2: joyful tenor, organ joins]
I had plans, I had a list
I had a calm that I haven't missed
You came along like a marching band
Now I'm clapping, and I don't understand

[Chorus: brass section, full voice, group answering]
Oh, I'm stuck on a good thing
Glued to a real thing
Nobody come and pull me free
I'm stuck on a good thing
Tied to the best thing
That ever went and happened to me

[Bridge: band drops to chant and handclaps]
Hubba-loo, hubba-loo-la
(All day long)
Hubba-loo, hubba-loo-la
(All night long)

[Final Chorus: key up a step, brass blazing, everyone]
Oh, I'm stuck on a good thing
Glued to a real thing
Nobody come and pull me free
I'm stuck on a good thing
Tied to the best thing
That ever went and happened to me

[Outro: chant alone, fading]
Hubba-loo, hubba-loo-la
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 118 BPM, 4/4, A-flat major, lifting a step for the last chorus. A galloping, grinning pop stomp.

VOICE: A male tenor with a bright, open, slightly theatrical voice who sounds as if he is smiling. A group of men chant the nonsense syllables in low unison, rhythmic and deadpan, at the start, under the verses and alone in the bridge.

INSTRUMENTS: A brass section (trumpets and trombones) playing big, cheerful fanfares in the chorus. A galloping drum beat with tom-toms. A bouncing electric bass. Electric organ. A bright rhythm guitar. Handclaps. Tambourine.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, the chant alone, then drums and bass join. 0:16 Verse 1. 0:36 Chorus 1 with brass. 1:00 Verse 2. 1:20 Chorus 2. 1:44 Bridge, chant and handclaps. 2:00 The key lifts for the final chorus. 2:28 Outro, the chant alone, fading by 2:50.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Mid-1970s European pop: bright, brassy and compressed, with the chant dry and upfront like a rhythm instrument.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The chant in the first three seconds.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The second verse belongs to someone who had a list and a calm and has cheerfully lost both. It fits a late romance or a grandchild as well as a first love.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Delight, more delight.
